doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Marriage, family and the Capitol albums
title: Songs that stay in her rotation
summary: She talks about Green Dolphin Street, Sleeping Bee and why good songs do not wear out.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: In addition to Guess Who I Saw Today, there are a lot of songs that are still in your rotation, if you want to call it that, today. I’m thinking about – I don’t know – Green Dolphin Street.
Never Will I Marry, Save Your Love for Me, Masquerade.
Yeah, that’s an easy one when you need something uptempo to break with.
Do you ever get tired of these songs?

I pick songs that are good. If you pick songs that are good, you don’t get tired of them. If you pick a song that works – especially with the rhythm section that I have, Sleeping Bee would be – with a bass player, when you have a great bass player, Sleeping Bee works every time. I don’t remember half of the material I’ve recorded. That’s for sure. People keep asking me, do you remember a certain – no, I don’t. And I don’t feel bad because I don’t. I can’t retain all of this. It’s impossible. When you realize how much there has been, there’s no way I could remember all of these things.
And yet I’ve heard you pull a few out of the hat.

That’s God. That’s not me, because I can’t remember – getting older is – my memory was never that great to begin with. In fact, because I didn’t – all of it was so natural that it didn’t register. Do you understand what I’m saying? It was a natural kind of thing, the work, the singing, the songs that were picked, and it wasn’t something that I gave a lot of thought to. It was just there.
So you don’t have to work at keeping material fresh for yourself or for the audience?
If I were working 40, even 36 weeks a year, maybe I would do a lot of changing. But I’m only working four times a year. What – no, I’m not . . .
At this point, I’m not going to . . .
Back then, if it was working, we left it alone.
What does it mean when you say, it worked, the song works?
It’s got a great story. It’s more than just singing notes. It’s telling a story.
